mn70:5.2: “Sir, we went to the mendicants who follow Assaji and Punabbasuka and said to them:
mn70:5.3: ‘Reverends, the Buddha never eats at night, and neither does the mendicant Saṅgha.
mn70:5.4: Doing so, they find that they’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.
mn70:5.5: You too should never eat at night.
mn70:5.6: Doing so, you’ll find that you’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.’
mn70:5.7: When we said this, sir, the mendicants who followed Assaji and Punabbasuka said to us,
mn70:5.8: ‘Reverends, we eat at dusk, at daybreak, and at the wrong time of day.
mn70:5.9: Doing so, we find that we’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.
mn70:5.10: Why should we give up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time?
mn70:5.11: We shall eat at dusk, at daybreak, and at the wrong time of day.’
mn70:5.12: Since we were unable to persuade the mendicants who follow Assaji and Punabbasuka, sir, we are reporting this matter to the Buddha.”
mn70:28.1: The elephant, Rāhula, the world as eternal,
mn70:28.2: Māluṅkyaputta, and the one named Bhaddāli;
mn70:28.3: the little bird, and the request of Sahampati,
mn70:28.4: Nāḷaka, the wilderness monk, and the one named Kīṭāgiri.
